issues.legal_issue: A preliminary decree in a partition suit survives a consolidation notification when no appeal against that decree is pending, even though proceedings to prepare or appeal the final decree abate.
material_facts: A preliminary decree in a partition suit had determined the parties’ rights and shares in the land.
No appeal against the preliminary decree was pending when the consolidation notification was issued; proceedings concerning the final decree were pending.
Consolidation authorities relied on the preliminary decree in resolving the parties’ claims.
issues.conclusion: The preliminary decree remains unaffected, while proceedings relating to preparation of the final decree abate; consolidation authorities may give effect to the surviving decree under Sections 9 and 9A of the Act.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 5(2) of the U.P. Consolidation of Holdings Act, proceedings concerning declaration or determination of rights in land abate upon the prescribed order, and the affected rights may be pursued before consolidation authorities under Section 5(2)(b). Read with Section 2(2) and Order 20 Rule 18 of the Code of Civil Procedure, a preliminary partition decree determines and declares the parties’ rights, while the final decree works out those rights. Sections 97 CPC, Order 26 Rules 13 and 14 CPC, and the principles in Ahmed Musaji Saleji v. Hashim Ebrahim Saleji, Venkata Reddy v. Pothi Reddy, Gyarsi Bai v. Dhansukh Lal, and Shankar Balwant Lokhande v. Chandrakant Shankar Lokhande support treating an unappealed preliminary decree as final on the matters it decides. The court approved Ruderpal Singh, Satish Kumar and Mohan Lal and disapproved Ram Garib on this point.

rule.if: consolidation_proceeding and consolidation_notification_published and partition_suit and preliminary_decree_already_passed and preliminary_decree_not_under_appeal and final_decree_proceedings_pending

predicates.consolidation_proceeding: The matter concerns proceedings affected by the commencement of consolidation operations over land.
predicates.consolidation_notification_published: A notification commencing consolidation operations was published for the area containing the land.
predicates.partition_suit: The underlying suit seeks division of jointly held land and determination of the parties’ shares.
predicates.preliminary_decree_already_passed: The court had passed a preliminary decree declaring the parties’ rights or shares before the notification was published.
predicates.preliminary_decree_not_under_appeal: No appeal challenging the preliminary decree was pending when the notification was published.
predicates.final_decree_proceedings_pending: Proceedings to implement the declared shares or challenge the final decree were pending when the notification was published.

issues.definition: When consolidation proceedings concern a partition suit with a previously passed preliminary decree that is not under appeal, and final-decree proceedings remain pending, the preliminary decree survives and may be given effect.

issues.legal_issue: A consolidation notification abates the entire partition suit, including its preliminary decree, when an appeal against that preliminary decree is pending.
material_facts: A preliminary decree had been passed in a partition suit.
An appeal challenging the preliminary decree was pending when the consolidation notification was issued.
issues.conclusion: The notification has the effect of abating the entire suit and proceedings, including the preliminary decree.
issues.legal_principle: Section 5(2)(a) of the U.P. Consolidation of Holdings Act provides for abatement of covered suits and proceedings pending before a court or authority, and Section 5(2)(b) preserves the right to agitate the disputed rights before consolidation authorities. The court relied on Ram Adhar Singh v. Ramroop Singh, Chattar Singh v. Thakur Prasad Singh, Munshi Muqbool Raza v. Hasan Raza, Satyanarayan Prasad Sah v. State of Bihar, and Mst. Bibi Rahmani Khatoon v. Harkoo Gope for the principle that pending proceedings abate; it distinguished cases where no appeal against the preliminary decree was pending.

issues.definition: When consolidation proceedings concern a partition suit and an appeal against its previously passed preliminary decree is pending at the time of notification, the entire suit and its proceedings abate.
